correctness.rationale: The universal-pair construction has weight six and satisfies both double Roman defense and total positive support. If both bipartition classes contain zeros, each side must carry either a label 3 or two labels 2, hence at least three units; equality forces one label 3 per side, and zero defense plus totality force universality. If zeros occur on only one side, the opposite side is entirely positive and the label-1 support condition raises the total to at least seven. If there are no zeros, weight six would mean all labels are one, which is invalid. The direct checker confirms the classification on all canonical chain types with side sizes three and four.
